kind: Keep a journal by the Church's day, and go deeper into every verse
title: Keep a journal by the Church's day, and go deeper into every verse
blurb: Purify 1.9 keeps a journal with you by the Church's day, free for everyone, and opens every verse: hold it to see its Greek, or, with Purify Plus, to study it with its cross-references, compare it across Bibles and remember it. Five more Bibles to download, in Russian, Greek, Serbian, Arabic and Spanish, and in Purify Plus new reading plans for the Nativity Fast, Holy Week, John, Acts and the whole New Testament.

items.text: Your journal, by the Church's day: today's page shows the day's feast or saints and its readings, each with a pen to begin a page about it. Write freely, add verse cards and your highlights, and quote anything in Purify into it with Quote in journal. Free for everyone.
Take your journal with you: it is in Export your library, and on the website you can print it or save it as a PDF.
Hold a verse to open it: highlight it, copy it, share it as a picture, write a note, and see its Greek.

Five more Bibles to download from the translations list, each read in its own numbering: the Russian Synodal (1876), the Greek Septuagint with the Patriarchal text (1904), the Serbian of Karadžić and Daničić (1868), the Arabic Van Dyck (1865) and the Spanish Reina-Valera (1909). The Arabic and the Spanish are Protestant translations, and are labelled so.

Psalms 113 to 115 are divided as the Septuagint divides them, like the rest of the Psalter. Your notes, highlights, saved and gathered verses, and the verse cards in your journal move with their verses.
A Remember the verse widget for your home screen, the same for every reader.
Listening: one card at rest and a small pill as you scroll, and your place kept in every book.
The Creed by council: the Symbol of Faith article by article, with the words the Council of Constantinople added lit. Find it in Theology.
This day in Church history: on the days an event of Orthodox History fell, it is on Today under the saint of the day, with its picture.
Orthodox History: the great events as large cards and the rest with their pictures, and every picture for every reader.
The history map puts each event where its own account says, Alaska and America among them.
In Purify Plus, study a verse with its cross-references, which now reach into the Old Testament in the Septuagint, and tap a word to study its Greek.
Compare, in Purify Plus: a verse in every Bible you can download and in the Greek, each at the place its own numbering puts it.
Remember the verse, in Purify Plus, in three steps: the missing words, then the first letters, then from memory, spaced over the days that follow.
New reading plans, in Purify Plus: John in 21 days, Acts in 28 days, the New Testament in a year, the Nativity Fast and Holy Week, nearly every day with a passage of the Fathers on it.
The plans page keeps your place, puts the season's plan at the top and shows every plan with its picture; the four Gospels plan now shows St John.
The full journal, in Purify Plus: covers from the icons, notebooks and tags, blocks and styles, and on a computer your notebooks at the side.
Share a journal page: a saved page goes out as a copy at a link of its own. Three a month for everyone, without limit in Purify Plus, and Stop sharing takes the copy down at once.
The Florilegium, in Purify Plus, renewed: your gatherings as cards, a line from them on Today, and four whole passages of Scripture to begin with. Hand a gathering on as a booklet.
If your Purify Plus ends, the gatherings in your Florilegium stay yours to read.
The Thread, in Purify Plus: 35 events of Orthodox History step by step on their maps, year by year.
Candlelight lights the lines you are reading with a soft glow and darkens the edges. Night reading turns it on in one tap, and it can come on by itself at Vespers, from your city's sunset.
Earn two palettes by reading: Councils, for every council's page read to the end, and Cappadocian, for a work by each of the three Cappadocian Fathers. Both are Purify Plus palettes.
Ambience: two sounds at once, each with its own volume, and the last sound you played remembered.

Listening offline, in Purify Plus: saved books marked in the list, a chant kept on your phone as a book is, each book's size shown before you save it, saving that waits for Wi-Fi and picks up after a lost signal, Settings, On this device, to see what is kept, and on Android the week's readings kept offline by themselves.
The shop's photos load as you browse, so the apps no longer carry them.
Every field's hint is easier to read on every palette, and in Candlelight the verses you are not reading are easier to read.
The day's prayer hours no longer fade: the hours that are not now step back in their words.
The reader's bars leave later and slower, and the mini player moves with them at their pace.
The words under the player's buttons fit in every language.
Saved says how to begin: bookmark a verse to keep it here. And Remember the verse goes by one name everywhere.
The Supporter mark explains itself when you tap it, and the sync preview shows an example instead of a zero.
Writing a new post in Community: the page folds its head again as you type.
The Dome light banner is now a soft light from above, and the gift box opens in a flood of light.
Small things put right: Try it's names fit on two lines, cathedral bells has its own icon, and Discord status is offered only in the Windows app, where it works.

What we count, as the privacy page promises to tell you here, each a total with no session, no account and no device in it: each welcome question reached and answered, with a note when you come back on your second, seventh and thirtieth day, and the kind of screen you were on when you put the app away. Both have been counted since 1.8.

New in 1.9, and totals too, never you: which Purify Plus feature you tapped and, if you then subscribed, whether for a month or a year; the Bibles downloaded, the plans begun and finished, the journal pages written and shared, and the app version in use; and, when we test two versions of a screen, which one a count came from.

The privacy page now names eight more things Purify counts, each as a total and never a person: a first prayer or chapter, the steps of a first week, where an account is made, reminders turned on or off, the steps of the Plus sheet, a device's first day, the two small cards on Today, and the first step opened. The Terms now say that two readers may at times be shown different versions of a screen.

What we keep, and for how long: a record of each Purify Plus purchase (the store, the plan, whether it is a free trial, the price, the dates, and why a membership ended), no longer linked to you once you delete your account; a short report when something fails, with nothing in it that names you, deleted after 14 days; a search that found nothing, without who you are, for 90 days; a report someone makes on a shared journal page, with their account, until the page stops being shared; and the anonymous visit data, kept with no date to delete it.

With Purify Plus, your plans' progress, Remember the verse's schedule, your place and your reading settings travel with your account, and are deleted with it. The privacy page and the terms now name the company that runs Purify, Purify Orthodox LLC: write to support@purifyapp.net for help and to legal@purifyapp.net for anything legal.

A saint's books in print no longer load their covers from Amazon, and our emails no longer load fonts from Google: opening them tells neither company anything. Amazon is reached only when you tap to buy.
